name: Pistachio and Blackberry Traybake
method: Beat the butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
Add the eggs to the butter mixture one at a time, whisking after each addition.
Fold in the ground almonds, blitzed pistachios, 80g of flour and lemon zest.
Toss the blackberries with 10g of flour, shaking off excess, and fold through batter.
Bake for 50 minutes to 1 hour at 180 degrees.

name: Pistachio Stuffed Cookies
method: Add 6 tbsps of pistachio spread to baking paper and freeze.
Add butter, both sugars and vanilla, beat together for 5 minutes.
Add 1 egg and 1 egg yolk and beat to combine.
Separately, mix flour, corn flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt.
Add dry ingredients to mixture with chopped chocolate and pistachios. Mix until no flour can be seen.
Divide dough into 6 pieces (~150g each).
Flatten a piece of cookie dough and wrap around frozen pistachio spread. Freeze for 1 hour.
Bake cookies for 20-22 minutes at 220 degrees.

name: Triple Chocolate Brownies
method: Melt dark chocolate with butter and espresso until smooth.
Mix flour, cocoa powder and a pinch of salt.
Beat eggs, sugar and vanilla. Fold in cooled chocolate mix then sift and fold in dry ingredients until just combined.
Add two thirds of milk and white chocolate, fold through briefly.
Add batter to tin and scatter remaining chocolate on top.
Bake for 30 minutes at 180 degrees.

name: Banana Bread
method: Whisk together mashed banana, maple syrup, coconut oil, eggs and vanilla.
Whisk together flours, bicarb, cinnamon, nutmeg and a pinch of salt.
Add dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and stir until just combined. Fold in walnuts.
Pour batter into tin and bake for 50 - 65 minutes at 180 degrees.

name: Salted Caramel Brownies
method: Melt butter and chocolate together.
Beat half the caramel with sea salt. Beat the rest of the caramel with sugar and eggs. Beat in the chocolate and butter.
Combine plain flour and cocoa powder then sift into chocolate mix. Mix until smooth.
Pour half the batter into the tin and drizzle salted caramel mixture on top. Add the remaining brownie batter on top and top with remainder of caramel.

name: Lemon and Poppy Seed Loaf Cake
method: Beat the butter and sugar together. Beat in each egg.
Fold in lemon zest, poppy seeds and yogurt.
Fold in flour and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Add to tin and bake for 50 minutes at 180 degrees.

name: Nigella Chocolate Cookies
method: Stir flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, bicarbonate and sea salt together.
Beat butter, sugars and vanilla until creamy.
Add spoonful of dry ingredients and beat, in 3 batches add in the rest of the ingredients. Beat vigorously then stir in chocolate chips.
Divide into 8 and sprinkle sea salt on top.
Bake for 12 minutes at 180 degrees.

name: Flapjacks
method: Melt butter in a pan.
Add golden syrup and sugar to the butter.
Once sugar dissolved, stir in oats.
Pack into baking tin and bake for 25 minutes at 150 degrees.

name: Easy millionaire’s shortbread
method: Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4. Lightly grease and line a 20-22cm square or rectangular baking tin with a lip of at least 3cm.
To make the shortbread, mix 250g plain flour and 75g caster sugar in a bowl. Rub in 175g softened butter until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
Knead the mixture together until it forms a dough, then press into the base of the prepared tin.
Prick the shortbread lightly with a fork and bake for 20 minutes or until firm to the touch and very lightly browned. Leave to cool in the tin.

To make the caramel, place 100g butter or margarine, 100g light muscovado sugar and the can of condensed milk in a pan and heat gently until the sugar has dissolved. Continually stir with a spatula to make sure no sugar sticks to the bottom of the pan. (This can leave brown specks in the caramel but won’t affect the flavour.)

Turn up the heat to medium high, stirring all the time, and bring to the boil, then lower the heat back to low and stirring continuously, for about 5-10 minutes or until the mixture has thickened slightly. Pour over the shortbread and leave to cool.
For the topping, melt 200g plain or milk chocolate slowly in a bowl over a pan of hot water. Pour over the cold caramel and leave to set. Cut into squares or bars with a hot knife.

name: Spiced apple and granola cake with salted honey buttercream
method: To make the apple puree for the cake, place the frozen Bramley apple slices (250 g) into a medium pan with a tablespoon of water. Cook over a medium heat for 15–20 minutes, until soft enough to purée, stirring occasionally to prevent it sticking and burning. Purée with a stick blender or in the small bowl of a food processor. Set aside.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan/gas mark 4. Line a loaf tin with greaseproof paper.

Beat the unsalted butter (115 g) and soft light brown sugar (100 g) until light and fluffy. Beat in the Scottish honey from highland heather (100 millilitre) and the large egg (1) and stir in the cooked apples.

In a separate bowl, sift the  plain flour (225 g), bicarbonate of soda (1 1/2 tsp), baking powder (1 tsp), ground cinnamon (1 tsp), ground ginger (1 tsp) and a generous pinch of salt. Fold the flour into the wet mixture. Stop mixing as soon as they are combined (it will be thick), then stir in the nut and raisin granola (100 g).
Scrape the batter into the lined tin. Bake for 40–50 minutes, or until an inserted skewer comes out clean and the surface of the cake feels springy when pressed. Cool in the tin.

Meanwhile, make the buttercream. Beat the salted butter (125 g) until light and fluffy, add the Scottish honey from highland heather (3 tbsp) and gradually beat in the icing sugar (200 g) until light and fluffy. Spread over the cake and scatter with nut and raisin granola (1 handful).

Meanwhile, make the buttercream. Beat the salted butter (125 g) until light and fluffy, add the Scottish honey from highland heather (3 tbsp) and gradually beat in the icing sugar (200 g) until light and fluffy. Spread over the cake and scatter with nut and raisin granola (1 handful).
